trigger: an operator follows the buf.yaml 'revert it' advice after a deletion has already shipped to agents or the gateway
summary: Recorded as the reporter stated it: IMPACT 'I1 (operability)', exposure 'documentation only' (recorded as unresolved, no closed value given), label NICE. The facts as stated (I1) read at HIGH under the stronger-of rule, so this row gates until resolved. Claim: the comment omits that reverting a deletion that already reached a release is itself a wire change; suggested 'if already released, treat revert as a new release'.

refuted_by: (1) I1 is defined as an authn/authz/confinement/crypto/audit control not holding; a proto-revert comment touches none. (2) 'Already shipped': every release tag (v0.14.0-rc5..rc7, v0.14.0, v0.14.1) is an ancestor of origin/main, and proto-compat (ci.yml:699) compares every PR against origin/main, so a deletion that reaches only dev was never in a release; an admin-bypassed one is caught again at the dev->main promotion. (3) 'Revert is wire-breaking': re-adding the item with its original number/name/type is additive; buf breaking passes additions (happy-path verified exit 0), and proto3 binaries treat an absent tag as unknown and skip/preserve it. Number reuse in between would itself need a deletion, which this policy blocks.
refuted_by_reporter: architect (independent Gate 8 adjudication; not the change author, not the reporter (sre), and not the party arguing the refutation; independence asserted, not enforced)
adjudicated_by: architect (owner of proto-compat truth; separation: Gate 7 'rejected/refuted at a derived HIGH' — not author, not raising agent, not the arguer)
adjudication_rationale: The recorded facts (I1) would gate at HIGH; the adjudicator found I1 inapplicable and both factual premises false, so no impact remains (impact restated empty, derives INFO). The buf.yaml comment stays as written.
summary: Refuted by independent architect adjudication; see refuted_by.
